# pbs_notification_endpoint_webhook (Resource)

Manages a Proxmox Backup Server webhook notification endpoint: an HTTP request PBS makes for every notification, to any service that takes one — a chat, a push service, an incident tool. A notification reaches an endpoint only through a matcher: route notifications to this one with a `pbs_notification_matcher` whose `target` names it.

`url`, the header values and `body` are [Handlebars](https://handlebarsjs.com) templates, rendered for each notification with `{{ title }}`, `{{ message }}`, `{{ severity }}`, `{{ timestamp }}`, the notification's metadata fields as `{{ fields.<name> }}` and the endpoint's secrets as `{{ secrets.<name> }}`, and the helpers `{{ url-encode … }}`, `{{ escape … }}` (for a JSON string) and `{{ json … }}`. In Terraform strings, write `{{` as is, but `${` as `$${`.

PBS does not contact the URL when it saves the endpoint; a wrong setting shows when PBS sends the first notification, or at once with `send_test_on_apply`. PBS goes through the HTTP proxy in the node's settings, when one is set, and treats any answer but a 2xx as a failure.

~> **PBS refuses to delete an endpoint a matcher targets.** When a change of `name` replaces an endpoint that a `pbs_notification_matcher` targets, set `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` on the endpoint, so that the matcher moves to the new endpoint before the old one goes.

Endpoint and matcher names share one namespace. Managing notification endpoints needs `Sys.Modify on /system/notifications`, reading them `Sys.Audit on /system/notifications`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Post every notification to a chat service's incoming webhook as JSON. The
# URL, the header values and the body are Handlebars templates;
# {{ escape ... }} makes a value safe inside a JSON string.
resource "pbs_notification_endpoint_webhook" "chat" {
  name   = "chat"
  url    = "https://chat.example.com/hooks/{{ secrets.hook_id }}"
  method = "post"
  header = [
    { name = "Content-Type", value = "application/json" },
    { name = "Authorization", value = "Bearer {{ secrets.token }}" },
  ]
  body = jsonencode({
    text = "[{{ severity }}] {{ escape title }}\n\n{{ escape message }}"
  })

  # The secrets' values are write-only: they never reach the plan or state,
  # and PBS never returns them. PBS receives a value when the secret is
  # created and whenever its value_wo_version changes; to rotate the token,
  # increment its version alone, and the hook ID keeps the value PBS has.
  secret = [
    { name = "hook_id", value_wo = var.chat_hook_id, value_wo_version = 1 },
    { name = "token", value_wo = var.chat_token, value_wo_version = 1 },
  ]

  send_test_on_apply = true
}

variable "chat_hook_id" {
  description = "ID of the chat's incoming webhook."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}

variable "chat_token" {
  description = "Token the chat's webhook accepts."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}

# Failed jobs of any kind go to the chat.
resource "pbs_notification_matcher" "errors_to_chat" {
  name           = "errors-to-chat"
  target         = [pbs_notification_endpoint_webhook.chat.name]
  match_severity = ["error"]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Endpoint name, 2 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, not starting with `.` or `-`. Matchers name it in `target`. Changing it replaces the endpoint.
- `url` (String) URL to send the request to, `http://` or `https://`, with an optional port; its path and query may use templates, such as `https://ntfy.example.com/{{ secrets.topic }}`. PBS checks the host and port.

### Optional

- `body` (String) Body of the request, a template, such as a JSON document; none when left out. Send it with a `Content-Type` header that says what it is. PBS stores it base64-encoded; the provider encodes and decodes it.
- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 128 characters on one line.
- `disable` (Boolean) Whether the endpoint is disabled: matchers that target it send nothing through it. Defaults to `false`.
- `header` (Attributes List) HTTP headers of the request, in order, such as `{ name = "Content-Type", value = "application/json" }`. A name may appear more than once. PBS stores the values base64-encoded; the provider encodes and decodes them. A header that holds a credential should take it from a secret, as `{{ secrets.<name> }}`: header values are stored as they are given and readable through the API. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--header))
- `method` (String) HTTP method: `post`, the default, `put` or `get`.
- `secret` (Attributes List) Secrets the templates of `url`, the headers and `body` can use as `{{ secrets.<name> }}`. PBS keeps them in a file only root reads, never returns their values, and masks the values in its logs and error messages — but only as they are: a value a helper such as `url-encode` changed is not masked, which the provider makes up for in the errors it shows. The values are write-only: Terraform passes them to PBS without storing them in the plan or state, so a change made outside Terraform goes unnoticed. PBS receives a secret's value when the secret is created — with the endpoint, or when it is added to the list — and whenever its `value_wo_version` changes; every other secret keeps the value PBS has. Removing a secret from the list removes it from PBS, and PBS's secrets that the list does not name show as a change that removes them. Needs Terraform or OpenTofu 1.11 or later. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--secret))
- `send_test_on_apply` (Boolean) Have PBS send a test notification through the endpoint after every apply that creates or changes it, unless it is disabled, so that a wrong setting fails the apply instead of going unnoticed until a real notification is lost. Defaults to `false`. It exists only in Terraform: turning it on changes nothing in PBS and sends nothing by itself, and every test delivers a real message. PBS waits up to 10 seconds for an answer. The test notification has severity `info` and no metadata fields: `{{ fields.<name> }}` renders empty, `{{ json fields.<name> }}` renders `null`, and `escape` or `url-encode` given one, such as `{{ escape fields.datastore }}`, fails the test. A failed test fails the apply. When the test after a create fails, the provider deletes the endpoint again, so the next apply creates and tests it again — should that delete fail too, the endpoint is kept and marked tainted; when the test after an update fails, the endpoint keeps the change, and the next apply tests again only if the endpoint changes again. Sending a test needs `Sys.Modify on /system/notifications`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `name`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.
- `origin` (String) Where the endpoint comes from: `user-created` for every webhook endpoint, as PBS has no built-in one.

<a id="nestedatt--header"></a>
### Nested Schema for `header`

Required:

- `name` (String) Header name, such as `Authorization`.
- `value` (String) Header value, a template, such as `Bearer {{ secrets.token }}`.


<a id="nestedatt--secret"></a>
### Nested Schema for `secret`

Required:

- `name` (String) Secret name, unique in the list: letters, digits, `_` and `-`.
- `value_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Value of the secret. Write-only: PBS receives it as `value_wo_version` says.
- `value_wo_version` (Number) Version of `value_wo`, which Terraform stores in its place. Change it — increment it, say — to send a new `value_wo`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_notification_endpoint_webhook.chat
  identity = {
    name = "chat"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Endpoint name, such as `webhook`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_notification_endpoint_webhook.chat
  id = "chat"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Webhook endpoints are imported by name. PBS returns the names of the
# secrets but never their values, so every value_wo_version is empty after an
# import, and the next apply sends every secret's value_wo.
terraform import pbs_notification_endpoint_webhook.chat chat
```
